description: A self hosted virtual browser that runs in docker and uses WebRTC.

sources.entry: Neko - Virtual browser that runs in docker and uses WebRTC. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: Neko is a self-hosted virtual browser that runs in Docker and streams a desktop to multiple users over WebRTC.
summary.what_it_does: Neko runs a full browser (or any Linux program, or a whole desktop environment) inside a Docker container and streams it to users over WebRTC. Multiple participants can connect to the same virtual session at once and share control, which the README presents as the main use case for watch parties, interactive presentations, and collaborative browsing. The README says it also supports built-in audio, and that the screen can be broadcast over RTMP. It can be run outside a container too, by connecting to an X server on a host. The README also mentions a Go backend and a Vue front end, plus a separate neko-rooms project for room management and an API for requesting rooms.
use_cases: run an interactive presentation others can control
remote support or teaching over a shared browser
embed a virtual browser in a web app
jump host access to internal apps without VPN
persistent or throwaway browser in a container
notable: Multi-participant shared control of one virtual browser session
Streams with WebRTC rather than image frames over WebSockets, per the README
Can run any Linux program or full desktop, not only a browser
Optional RTMP broadcast of the session
Apache-2.0 licensed fork lineage from an archived upstream project, per the README
caveats: README does not include install or run commands; setup details are in external documentation at neko.m1k1o.net
Room management and zero-knowledge HTTPS install are in a separate project (neko-rooms)
Some listed features, such as RDP/VNC support, are described in the README as future work
